$comment: Single source of truth for the OHL-901 digital twin: one 132 kV overhead line span with ACSR Drake 795 kcmil 26/7 conductor, a line monitor on the lower phase and a weather station. Conductor data from Southwire (ASTM B232); heat balance IEEE 738.

twin.kind: Overhead line span with line monitor (conductor temperature, current, LiDAR clearance) and weather station

standards.conductor: Southwire ACSR (ASTM B232) Drake 795 kcmil 26/7: OD 28.14 mm, 1.628 kg/m, RBS 140.1 kN, R_dc20 0.0702 ohm/km, R_ac75 0.0863 ohm/km
standards.thermal: IEEE Std 738 heat balance (Joule, solar, convective, radiative), steady state and transient; dynamic line rating at 75 C
standards.sag: Ruling-span change of state, parabolic approximation, elastic + thermal strain (no creep model); fitted as a cubic of conductor temperature
standards.information_model: Points named after IEC 61850 logical nodes (MMXU, STMP, MMET, GGIO)

identification.description: 132 kV overhead line 901, span 14-15 (lower phase L1)
identification.medium: Bare ACSR conductor, 350 m span, lattice towers

conductor.r_note: AC 75 C from the Southwire catalogue (0.0263 ohm/kft, 60 Hz); AC 25 C derived = DC 20 C x (1 + 0.00403 x 5) x the same AC/DC ratio
conductor.mech_note: typical 26/7 ACSR values, not from the Southwire table (UNVERIFIED)
conductor.surface_note: aged conductor (assumption; Southwire rates with emissivity 0.5)

line.assumed: 132 kV single circuit, 350 m level ruling span, everyday tension 20 % RBS at 20 C, lower phase attachment 19.5 m, azimuth 75 deg

ratings.static_basis: IEEE 738 at 75 C, 40 C ambient, 0.61 m/s wind at 90 deg, 1000 W/m2 (conservative seasonal assumptions)
ratings.check_note: this implementation with emissivity/absorptivity 0.5, 25 C, 0.61 m/s, 1000 W/m2 at 75 C; Southwire lists 907 A (their sun model may differ)

clearances.note: assumed minimum clearances for 132 kV (utility practice varies)

weather_model.solar: global irradiance x absorptivity x D (simplified vs. IEEE 738 solar position model)

monitor.line_monitor: Clamp-on line monitor modelled on the Lindsey TLM: conductor temperature, current, LiDAR clearance; second unit at the mid-span joint
monitor.weather: Weather station on tower 15 at conductor height
monitor.insulator: Leakage-current sensor on the tower 15 L1 insulator string
monitor.vibration: Aeolian vibration recorder at the tower 14 suspension clamp (bending amplitude, IEEE 1368 method)

demo.note: The plant clock runs 30x real time (one day in 48 min): the conductor's ~20 min thermal time constant plays out in about 40 s, so weather and load changes are visible during a demo.

points.label: Mid-span compression joint temperature (second line monitor)
Distance to the nearest vegetation below the span (LiDAR)
Insulator string leakage current (peak, tower 2 L1)
Aeolian vibration, bending amplitude p-p at 89 mm from the clamp

limits.basis: joint delta-T after NETA MTS infrared guidance (typical, unverified); leakage-current and vibration (IEEE 1368 safe bending amplitude for ACSR) limits are typical public values, assumed

joint_hotspot.label: Mid-span joint degradation
joint_hotspot.cause: A compression joint loses contact (corrosion, poor crimp): its resistance rises, so it runs hotter than the conductor next to it, more so at high current, until it fails
joint_hotspot.action: Thermographic check from the ground or air; replace the joint (or add a shunt sleeve) at the next outage

conductor_creep.label: Excess sag (conductor creep)
conductor_creep.cause: The aluminium has crept or the conductor was overstretched in a past overload: the span sags more than its temperature explains
conductor_creep.action: Survey the span; re-sag (re-tension) the conductor and check the clearance at the maximum operating temperature

vegetation_encroachment.label: Vegetation encroachment
vegetation_encroachment.cause: Trees below the span grow into the clearance zone; on a hot afternoon the sagging conductor gets closer still
vegetation_encroachment.action: Raise a vegetation work order: trim or remove the trees below the span

insulator_pollution.label: Insulator pollution
insulator_pollution.cause: Dust, salt or industrial deposits on the insulator string become conductive when wet: leakage current rises, most at dawn when the humidity is high
insulator_pollution.action: Wash the insulators (live washing) or replace them with silicone / RTV-coated units

overload_beyond_dlr.label: Overload beyond the dynamic rating
overload_beyond_dlr.cause: The current exceeds what today's weather can cool: the conductor heats past its maximum operating temperature, sags towards the ground and anneals the aluminium
overload_beyond_dlr.action: Re-dispatch or switch to cut the flow below the dynamic rating; inspect for annealing after a long excursion

damper_loss.label: Vibration damper lost
damper_loss.cause: A Stockbridge damper has slipped or lost a weight: aeolian vibration in steady low winds grows and fatigues the strands at the clamp
damper_loss.action: Replace or reposition the damper; inspect the strands at the suspension clamp

sensor_fault.label: Conductor temperature sensor fault
sensor_fault.cause: The line monitor's temperature probe has lost contact: it reads low, while the heat balance and the measured sag both say the conductor is hotter
sensor_fault.action: Do not trust the sensor for ratings: fall back to the heat-balance temperature, then service the line monitor

compare.label: Conductor temperature
compare.basis: IEEE 738 steady heat balance at the live current and weather

compare.label: Dynamic line rating
compare.basis: IEEE 738 at 75 °C with the live weather (static rating 725 A)

compare.label: Ground clearance
compare.basis: 19.5 m attachment − sag at the measured conductor temperature (change of state)

compare.label: Temperature from sag
compare.basis: conductor temperature that explains the measured sag

design.label: Conductor
design.value: ACSR Drake 795 kcmil 26/7 (ASTM B232): OD 28.14 mm, 1.628 kg/m, RBS 140 kN, Rac75 0.0863 Ω/km

design.label: Span
design.value: 132 kV single circuit, 350 m ruling span, 20 % RBS at 20 °C, attachment 19.5 m (assumed)

design.label: Ratings
design.value: 75 °C continuous / 100 °C emergency (Southwire); static 725 A at 40 °C, 0.61 m/s, full sun

design.label: Source
design.value: Southwire ACSR data (SPEC 80100, Drake product page); IEEE 738; 3D built procedurally, not manufacturer CAD
